videoSettings.bitrateCeiling: A ceiling for motion (video, scrolling); a still screen sends far less. Auto follows the mode; Economy suits remote and mobile connections.
videoSettings.codecHint: H.265 needs about a third less traffic for the same picture; H.264 plays in more browsers.

videoSettings.deviceTransportHint: For an administrator it is also the device transport: browsers without a choice of their own start with it, and RustDesk accepts WebRTC only with WebRTC.
videoSettings.deviceTransport: The device transport is {{transport}}: browsers without a choice of their own start with it, and RustDesk follows it.

transportHint.direct: H.264/H.265 over HTTPS, decoded by the browser. Lowest latency.
transportHint.webrtc: Works in most browsers and across networks; encrypted with SRTP.
transportHint.mjpeg: A JPEG image per frame: the most compatible, the most traffic.

reason.video-memory: needs more video memory: restart the device to use the updated system
reason.receiver: not supported by this HDMI receiver

reason.mjpeg-4k: not available while the HDMI input is 3840 × 2160, use H.264 or H.265

videoSettings.mjpegChromaHint: 4:2:2 preserves more color detail and can increase frame size. The choice is saved and applies without a restart.
videoSettings.hevcDirectHint: The encoder reads the captured picture itself instead of a converted copy: lower latency (about 6 ms at 1080p, 25 ms at 4K) and less memory traffic. Turn off to encode through the video processor as before. Applies within a second without a restart.
videoSettings.viDirectH264Hint: H.264 at the input size and rate reads the captured picture itself: the capture switches to 4:2:0 color sampling (at 1080p about 6 ms lower latency and less memory traffic), and MJPEG also uses 4:2:0 meanwhile. The capture restarts briefly when this mode changes. Turn off to encode through the video processor as before.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_resolution: MJPEG is limited to 1920 pixels in width to preserve 4:2:2 while H.264/H.265 uses a wider output. The selected resolution resumes when that video stream ends.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_video: Only one capture output supports widths above 1920 pixels. MJPEG uses 4:2:0 while both streams are wider; 4:2:2 resumes when the video stream ends or either stream is reduced.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_frameDetection: Turn off frame detection to use 4:2:2.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_diagnostic: 4:2:2 is unavailable in the current capture mode.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_hardware: Capture fell back to 4:2:0 after an error. Retry 4:2:2 when the signal is stable.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_h264Capture: The capture runs in 4:2:0 for H.264 straight from capture, so MJPEG uses 4:2:0 too. 4:2:2 returns when the capture switches back, for example for H.265 or a scaled H.264 stream.
videoSettings.mjpegChromaFallback_pending: 4:2:2 will apply to the next captured frame.
videoSettings.cubeMonitorHint: Cube/Lite: writes and verifies the EDID. Physically disconnect all power sources and reconnect to apply it; a software reboot is not sufficient. The monitor keeps the fastest refresh rate of the chosen resolution, and the frame rate only limits the stream.
videoSettings.powerCycleConfirm: Only continue if you can physically disconnect all power sources from the NanoKVM after writing. Video may be interrupted until then. Rebooting through software does not apply this change.
videoSettings.powerCycleWritten: EDID written and verified. Disconnect and reconnect NanoKVM power to apply.
videoSettings.powerCyclePendingHint: An EDID write was attempted. Disconnect all power sources and reconnect the NanoKVM. This reminder survives software reboots; dismiss it only after the physical power cycle.
videoSettings.powerCycleAckConfirm: Confirm that you physically disconnected all power sources and reconnected the NanoKVM. This only dismisses the reminder; it does not restart the device.
videoSettings.directSmoothHint: Adaptively buffers frames to smooth uneven delivery, adding a small delay.
videoSettings.directImmediateHint: Displays frames as soon as they are decoded. Uneven delivery can cause visible stutter.

tips.title: How to upload
tips.usb1: Connect the NanoKVM to your computer via USB.
tips.usb2: Ensure that the virtual disk is mounted (Settings - Virtual disk).
tips.usb3: Open the virtual disk on your computer and copy the image file to the root directory of the virtual disk.
tips.scp1: Make sure the NanoKVM and your computer are on the same local network.
tips.scp2: Open a terminal on your computer and use the SCP command to upload the image file to the /data directory on the NanoKVM.
tips.tf1: This method is supported on Linux system
tips.tf2: Get TF card from the NanoKVM (for the FULL version, disassemble the case first).
tips.tf3: Insert the TF card into a card reader and connect it to your computer.
tips.tf4: Copy the image file to the /data directory on the TF card.
tips.tf5: Insert the TF card into the NanoKVM.

identity.title: USB identity
identity.description: What the computer sees in the device descriptor: vendor and product IDs, manufacturer and product names. For hosts whose USB policy or endpoint security objects to "NanoKVM".

invalid.id: IDs are four hexadecimal digits like 0x1234, not 0x0000.
invalid.string: Names are 1 to 126 printable ASCII characters without leading or trailing spaces.
invalid.serial: A serial number is 1 to 126 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.

identity.idWarning: A vendor or product ID other than the factory one is yours to answer for. Linux hosts set up with the serial console helper no longer match the NanoKVM (its udev rule names the IDs).
identity.serialHint: Empty: the chip UID. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. Linux hosts set up with the serial console helper match it: run its apply again after a change.

userDisk.title: User disk
userDisk.description: A writable FAT32 drive the computer sees next to the virtual CD/disk: BIOS update files, profiles, logs. Stored on the SD card.
userDisk.needsDisk: Enable the virtual disk to get the user disk; it is a third drive of the same USB device.

states.pending: On; appears on the computer once the USB devices reconnect

userDisk.deleteConfirm: The image and everything on it are removed from the SD card.
userDisk.reconnect: The USB devices reconnect, so the computer loses and regains the NanoKVM drives for a moment.
userDisk.ejectFirst: Eject the drive on the computer first, so nothing is left half-written; then the USB devices reconnect.
userDisk.turnOffFirst: Turn the user disk off first.
userDisk.busy: The disk is busy. Wait for the current operation and try again.
userDisk.missing: The user disk image is gone. Create it again.
userDisk.notice: Mounting or ejecting a CD/disk image reconnects the USB devices too; the computer sees the user disk again afterwards with what it wrote. The whole image is allocated on the SD card at creation, so the large sizes take a while.

files.title: Files on the user disk
files.host: Eject this drive on the computer, then turn the user disk off above to manage its files.
files.hint: Turn the user disk on above when finished to make the files available to the computer. Existing files are never overwritten.
files.transferring: Transferring and saving… Wait for completion before connecting the disk.
files.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}}? Only empty folders can be deleted.

errors.host: The computer owns the disk. Eject it and turn it off above.
errors.busy: The disk is busy. Wait for the current operation and try again.
errors.exists: A file or folder with this name already exists.
errors.missing: The disk, file or folder no longer exists. Refresh or go up.
errors.space: Not enough free space, or the file exceeds FAT32’s 4 GiB minus 1 byte limit.
errors.io: The operation failed. Check the disk and system logs, then refresh.

serialConsole.title: Headless Linux console
serialConsole.description: A script on this NanoKVM sets up a login on its USB serial port on the connected computer. It reads the system first, refuses when it cannot do that safely, keeps backups and can undo its changes.
serialConsole.fromNetwork: Over the network, in a shell on the computer, as root:
serialConsole.fromUsbNetwork: Over the USB network, when the computer has no other network:
serialConsole.withWget: With wget instead of curl (Alpine, busybox):
serialConsole.diskAttached: The helper disk "NanoKVM Setup Disk" is attached to the computer as a read-only drive. Without a network:
serialConsole.diskPending: The helper disk appears on the computer once the USB devices reconnect.
serialConsole.diskStale: The helper disk was updated; the computer sees the new one once the USB devices reconnect.
serialConsole.diskNeedsDisk: Enable the virtual disk as well to get the helper disk: a read-only drive with the script, for a computer without a network.
serialConsole.applyHint: The command only reports. Add "apply" to make the changes and "undo" to remove them again.
serialConsole.testFailed: The console test could not run.

states.login: A login prompt answers on the serial port.
states.password: A password prompt answers: a login is in progress on the serial port.
states.shell: A shell session is open on the serial port.
states.text: The computer sent something, but no login prompt.
states.silent: No answer within 5 seconds: the computer has no login on the serial port yet, or USB serial is not connected.
states.busy: The USB serial console is open in the terminal. Close it and try again.
states.unavailable: USB serial is not enabled on this NanoKVM.
states.error: The serial port could not be read.

kvm.title: KVM
kvm.description: Keyboard, both mouse modes and the virtual disk: what a new device starts with. No network adapter appears on the computer.

standard.title: KVM + network
standard.description: Keyboard, both mouse modes, virtual disk and the USB network adapter. Leaves no room for the serial console.

console.title: KVM + serial console
console.description: Keyboard, both mouse modes, virtual disk and the serial console with its helper disk. Leaves no room for the USB network.

headless.title: Headless server
headless.description: The serial console and the virtual disk with its helper disk, which carries the script that sets up the serial login, so the server needs no network. No keyboard or mouse appears on the computer. Enabling RustDesk switches to its preset and disconnects the serial console.

remote.title: RustDesk
remote.description: Keyboard, both mouse modes, virtual disk and USB audio: what turning RustDesk on switches to, and turning it off goes back from. The computer gets a second speaker.

control.title: Keyboard and mouse only
control.description: Keyboard, relative mouse and absolute pointer, nothing else.

compatibilityProfile.title: HID-only compatibility profile (USB 1.1)
compatibilityProfile.description: Older descriptors for firmware and hosts that reject the composite device: keyboard and pointers only, without network, disk, serial helper disk or audio.

usb.updateFailed: Failed to update the USB composition.

relative.title: Relative mouse
relative.description: Pointer-lock mouse for firmware, installers and games

absolute.title: Absolute pointer
absolute.description: Direct screen-coordinate mapping without pointer drift

network.title: Virtual network
network.description: NCM network adapter on the remote host

disk.description: Present a mounted image as a USB drive

audio.title: USB audio
audio.description: Stereo audio output for the connected computer (48 kHz, 16-bit)

serial.title: USB serial console

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate the device presents over HTTPS. One from your own CA or a public one removes the browser warning.
certificate.pending: The certificate on disk is not the one served yet
certificate.subject: Subject
certificate.uploadHint: PEM files: the certificate with its chain and the unencrypted private key, as one file or two. New connections use it at once; HTTPS does not restart.
certificate.uploadConfirm: New connections get it at once. If the browser does not trust it, the next page load shows a warning; the generated certificate can be restored here.
certificate.removeConfirm: The uploaded certificate and private key are deleted from the device.
certificate.removed: The generated certificate is in use
certificate.offNote: HTTPS is off; the certificate is used once it is turned on.

acme.title: Let's Encrypt / ACME
acme.description: A certificate from a public certificate authority, issued and renewed by acme.sh on the device.
acme.installHint: Downloads the latest stable release from GitHub (about 1 MB).
acme.installConfirm: The latest stable release is downloaded from github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh. The account and the issued certificate are kept.
acme.removeConfirm: Renewal stops and the certificate and key are deleted from the device. HTTPS returns to the generated certificate. acme.sh and the account stay.
acme.domainsHint: The names the certificate is for; the first one is the main name. Wildcards (*.example.org) need the DNS challenge.
acme.emailHint: For the CA account: expiry notices. ZeroSSL requires it.
acme.challengeHttpHint: The CA fetches a token from http://<domain>/.well-known/acme-challenge/ on this device: port 80 must be reachable from the Internet at that name.
acme.challengeDnsHint: acme.sh adds a TXT record through the provider API. The credentials are stored by acme.sh for renewals (0600) and are never shown again.
acme.wildcardNeedsDns: A wildcard name needs the DNS challenge.
acme.providerDocs: How to get the credentials for {{name}}
acme.dnsSleepHint: Empty: acme.sh checks the record itself. Set when the provider is slow to publish.
acme.issueConfirmHttp: acme.sh asks the CA to fetch a token over port 80. The result appears below in a minute; the certificate is used for HTTPS at once, without a restart. Issuing again for the same names counts against the CA rate limits (Let’s Encrypt: 5 per week).
acme.issueConfirmDns: acme.sh adds a TXT record at the provider and waits for it. The result appears below within a few minutes; the certificate is used for HTTPS at once, without a restart. Issuing again for the same names counts against the CA rate limits (Let’s Encrypt: 5 per week).
acme.issueHint: Runs in the background; the page shows the result.
acme.uninstallConfirm: acme.sh, the CA account, the issued certificate and the settings are deleted. HTTPS returns to the generated certificate.

rustdesk.temporaryHint: Share this ID and password. The password changes when RustDesk starts or when you request a new one.
rustdesk.rotatingTemporaryHint: Share this ID and the current password. Each new successful sign-in generates a new password without closing active sessions. RustDesk also replaces it on startup or when you request a new one.
rustdesk.startForPassword: Enable RustDesk and save settings to generate a password.
rustdesk.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new password? Current RustDesk connections will close.
rustdesk.audioEnabled: USB audio is enabled. Select NanoKVM as the audio output on the connected computer. Sound can be muted in the RustDesk client.
rustdesk.audioDisabled: To stream computer sound, enable USB audio in the device USB settings and select NanoKVM as the audio output on the computer.
rustdesk.webrtcOn: Accepted: the video transport is WebRTC.
rustdesk.webrtcOff: Not accepted: the video transport is {{transport}}; RustDesk uses TCP and relay.
rustdesk.transportHint: Follows the transport in Settings > Video: WebRTC lets RustDesk accept WebRTC connections, Direct and MJPEG keep TCP and relay. WebRTC uses the STUN and TURN servers of the video stream and may reduce the frame rate on NanoKVM. The RustDesk 1.5 client does not try TCP in a round that offers WebRTC: to connect by ID over TCP, turn WebRTC off in the client too.
rustdesk.keepPassword: Leave empty to keep the current password
rustdesk.inputDefaults: Turning remote access on switches USB to the RustDesk composition (keyboard, both mouse modes, virtual disk and, with sound, USB audio); turning it off restores the previous one, unless it was changed in the meantime.
rustdesk.audioHint: Enables USB audio automatically. Select NanoKVM as the sound output on the connected computer.
rustdesk.audioMuted: Sound transmission through RustDesk is disabled.
rustdesk.unavailable: RustDesk is not available in the configured APK repositories. Add the repository containing nanokvm-rustdesk, or install its APK through Packages.
rustdesk.explain: Connect a RustDesk client to this ID to view HDMI and control USB keyboard and mouse.
rustdesk.video: Video automatically uses the codec selected in NanoKVM video settings. H.265 requires client support. Reconnect after changing the device codec. Browser takeover releases RustDesk input.

bmc.title: Redfish and IPMI
bmc.description: Power control of the host for data centre tools, through the ATX connection: Redfish (fence_redfish, Ansible) is part of NanoKVM OS, IPMI over LAN (ipmitool, fence_ipmilan) comes with an add-on.

bmc.redfishHint: At https://{{host}}/redfish/v1, with the BMC account below.

recovery.title: Backup & reset
recovery.scope: Back up managed NanoKVM OS settings and supported add-on settings. OS files, installed binaries, disk images and personal files are excluded. Custom configuration of other APK software is not reset.
recovery.encryption: The archive contains passwords and private keys. It is encrypted with your backup password (12–256 bytes). Keep the file and password somewhere safe; a lost password cannot be recovered.
recovery.archivePassword: Backup password (also used to open an archive)
recovery.updateBase: Update nanokvm-base to enable restore and reset.
recovery.fileLimit: Choose a settings archive up to 4 MiB.
recovery.device: Restore this device, including access and network settings
recovery.migrationHint: Migration keeps the destination’s users, identity, network, VPN, certificates and hardware settings. App binaries are not restored; install missing packages from Software.
recovery.keepUsers: Keep users, passwords and authorized SSH keys
recovery.keepApps: Keep all installed apps, including APK packages
recovery.resetHint: App settings are reset even when apps are kept. The installed OS version and personal files remain. Network settings are reset: connect by Ethernet/DHCP afterwards.
recovery.resetUsers: Without Keep users, web login returns to admin / admin with a required password change. Root password login is locked and SSH is disabled.
recovery.disconnect: The device will reboot and disconnect. Restoring network or access settings may change its address and login. Export a backup first.
recovery.removePackages: Optional APK roots to remove (unused dependencies may also be removed)
recovery.inventory: Packages recorded in the backup (not installed automatically)
recovery.confirm: I reviewed the changes and can reconnect to the device after reboot.
recovery.rebooting: Recovery queued. The device is rebooting; reconnect afterwards.
